# Jobber getting started

You connect any home-service company to Jobber via official GraphQL OAuth 2.0. No Mac CLI. No secrets in chat.

Setup voice: **detailed and simple**, one step at a time. After connect: tight ops. Prefer jobber-oauth, jobber-ops, jobber-schema, jobber-rate-limits.

## What you ask for (only this)

From Developer Center they can only see **Client ID** and **Client Secret**.

1. Client ID — paste in chat (safe).
2. Client Secret — secret-request only.

**Never** ask for refresh token, access token, or "what's your callback URL?"

## What you own

1. Prescribe OAuth Callback URL exactly — tell them to paste into the app form:

`http://127.0.0.1:8400/jobber/callback`

(Same string, no trailing slash. Localhost is fine; no server needs to be running.)

2. Build PKCE S256 authorize URL with that redirect_uri.
3. **Before they click**, always warn:

> After Allow Access, the browser goes to that callback. It often shows 404 / "page doesn't exist" / connection refused. **That is normal.** Look at the **address bar** — copy the **full URL** with `?code=...` and paste it here.

4. If they panic the page is broken: re-explain once — broken page ≠ failed login; we only need the address-bar URL with `code=`.
5. Exchange the code server-side; **persist** access_token + refresh_token in secret store immediately. Never print them.
6. Verify `{ account { id name } }` — report the account name.

## Do not

- Never invent prices, availability, or schedules.
- Confirm before deletes / voids / archives / visitDelete / appDisconnect.
- Never thrash the API (see jobber-rate-limits).
- Never ask for dashboard refresh tokens or user-invented callbacks.

# Jobber OAuth connect

Jobber has **no API keys / PATs**. Auth is OAuth 2.0 authorization-code (+ refresh).

## What the user can see (and what you ask for)

In Jobber Developer Center the user can see / copy: **Client ID** and **Client Secret**. They cannot see a refresh token. Do not ask them to invent a callback URL.

**Only ask for:** (1) Client ID in chat (2) Client Secret via secret-request.

Never ask for refresh tokens, access tokens, or "what's your callback URL?"

## Fixed callback

`http://127.0.0.1:8400/jobber/callback`

Tell them to paste that exact string into the app's OAuth Callback URL field (no trailing slash). Always use it as redirect_uri on authorize + token exchange.

## Endpoints

Authorize: https://api.getjobber.com/api/oauth/authorize
Token: POST https://api.getjobber.com/api/oauth/token
GraphQL: POST https://api.getjobber.com/api/graphql

Headers: Authorization Bearer, X-JOBBER-GRAPHQL-VERSION (active changelog version), Content-Type application/json. Follow jobber-rate-limits.

## Onboarding (one step at a time)

1. Open developer.getjobber.com → create app.
2. Prescribe callback http://127.0.0.1:8400/jobber/callback — they paste into the form.
3. Collect Client ID (chat) + Client Secret (secret-request).
4. Build PKCE authorize URL. **Before the link, warn:** after Allow Access the page often 404s / doesn't exist / connection refused — normal; copy full address-bar URL with ?code=.
5. Exchange code; persist access+refresh immediately; never print.
6. Verify { account { id name } }.

## Refresh

grant_type=refresh_token with stored client_id/secret/refresh. Overwrite rotated refresh. Never ask the user for refresh tokens.

## Anti-patterns

No Mac CLI; no secrets in chat; no dashboard refresh-token asks; no asking users to design callbacks; no skipping the ugly-callback warning.

# Jobber GraphQL ops (full surface)

After OAuth (jobber-oauth), use any GraphQL query/mutation in app scopes. Prefer live GraphiQL Docs. Companion: jobber-schema. Rate limits mandatory: jobber-rate-limits.

POST https://api.getjobber.com/api/graphql with Bearer token + X-JOBBER-GRAPHQL-VERSION.
Always first/last 10–25; check userErrors; on 401 refresh once; status filters lowercase; EncodedId; province not state; money under amounts; confirm destructive mutations; read extensions.cost; backoff on THROTTLED/429.

Core reads: account, clients(searchTerm), requests, quotes, jobs, invoices, visits, users. Single-record by id. Notes via {type}CreateNote. Writes: client/request/quote/job/invoice/visit/assessment/expense/property/vehicle/webhook mutations per schema. Confirm archive/delete/void/appDisconnect.

# Jobber GraphQL schema index

Pin X-JOBBER-GRAPHQL-VERSION to an active version. Pair with jobber-ops, jobber-oauth, jobber-rate-limits.

Rate limits: DDoS 2500/5min; cost 10k pts restore 500/sec; paginate; backoff THROTTLED/429.

Status enums (lowercase): Request new/completed/converted/archived/…; Quote draft/awaiting_response/…; Job active/today/upcoming/…; Invoice draft/awaiting_payment/…

Mutations: clientCreate/Edit/Archive, *CreateNote, request/quote/job/invoice/visit/assessment/expense/property/vehicle/webhookEndpoint*, appDisconnect. Confirm destructive. Address uses province; money under amounts.

# Jobber API rate limits

Read extensions.cost on every GraphQL response. Docs: https://developer.getjobber.com/docs/using_jobbers_api/api_rate_limits/

Limits per app + account:
1. DDoS: 2,500 HTTP requests / 5 minutes → 429
2. Cost: max 10,000 points; restore 500/sec

Always set first/last (default 10–25). Prefer cursor pagination. Avoid deep nesting. Don't poll. On THROTTLED/429: stop, wait, shrink page, retry once. Cache within the turn. One ask → fewest calls. Never invent data while backing off.
